mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has risen for four consecutive weekly means (-48.7 to -41.3). This momentum reflects an ongoing recovery trajectory as households gradually resume discretionary shopping trips, and the trend is expected to persist, pushing the next 28-day mean above the last 28-day mean.
evidence_refs: fact:four consecutive weekly increases in RETAIL_REC
failure_condition: The next 28-day RETAIL_REC mean is equal to or lower than the last 28-day mean despite the four-week rising streak continuing unbroken.

mechanism_narrative: If TRANSIT mobility crosses above -69 percent from baseline (a threshold signaling meaningful easing of movement restrictions on public transport use), this will coincide with increased willingness to travel for shopping and recreation, lifting RETAIL_REC over the following two weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT rises above -69 percent from baseline in a weekly mean
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT improved from -72.1 to -69.0 over four weeks
failure_condition: TRANSIT crosses above -69 but RETAIL_REC fails to rise or declines over the subsequent two weeks.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous improvement in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT indicates a joint return of commuting and work-based travel patterns. When both series rise together, the combined effect on incidental retail footfall (lunch trips, post-work errands) is larger than either alone, driving a stronger four-week increase in RETAIL_REC than either series predicts individually.
candidate_trigger: both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT rise week-on-week for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES rose from -43.0 to -37.7 and TRANSIT rose from -72.1 to -69.0 over four weeks
regime_hint: simultaneous easing of work and transit restrictions
failure_condition: WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both rise for two consecutive weeks but RETAIL_REC's four-week mean does not increase beyond what WORKPLACES alone would predict.

mechanism_narrative: While underlying mobility indices are improving, Greater Sydney remains under a public health lockdown order restricting non-essential retail operation as of the snapshot date. As long as this regulatory regime persists, retail capacity constraints will cap RETAIL_REC growth regardless of behavioral intent, keeping the next 28-day mean close to or below the last 28-day mean.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC remains deeply negative (-41.3) despite four weeks of improvement
regime_hint: lockdown restrictions (public health order) in effect
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC's next 28-day mean rises clearly above the last 28-day mean while lockdown restrictions remain formally in place and unchanged.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL mobility has declined for four consecutive weeks (22.3 to 20.0), indicating households are spending incrementally less time confined at home. This behavioral shift toward external activity is expected to translate into increased discretionary retail visits over the next two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL fell from 22.3 to 20.0 over four weeks
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL continues its decline for two more weeks but RETAIL_REC's mean does not rise over the corresponding period.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility has risen sharply (-31.6 to -16.9) consistent with the onset of Southern Hemisphere spring in September, encouraging outdoor recreation. This seasonal substitution effect diverts discretionary trips away from indoor retail and recreation venues, suppressing RETAIL_REC growth over the coming week.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS rose from -31.6 to -16.9 over four weeks
failure_condition: PARKS continues rising over the next week but RETAIL_REC also rises rather than stagnating or falling.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM mobility has nearly returned to baseline (-5.0), suggesting essential-goods shopping has saturated its recovery ceiling under current restrictions. If GROCERY_PHARM crosses above -5 percent, it signals that remaining retail suppression is structural (policy-driven) rather than demand-driven, implying RETAIL_REC recovery will stall rather than accelerate over the next week.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM rises above -5 percent from baseline
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM improved from -11.6 to -5.0 over four weeks
regime_hint: lockdown restrictions (public health order) in effect
failure_condition: GROCERY_PHARM crosses above -5 percent yet RETAIL_REC's mean rises over the following week.

mechanism_narrative: Rising PARKS use combined with a declining RESIDENTIAL share indicates a substitution pattern where people reallocate newly freed outdoor time to parks rather than retail. When both PARKS rises and RESIDENTIAL falls simultaneously, the interaction suppresses retail footfall growth more than either trend alone, producing a flat-to-negative movement in RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises and RESIDENTIAL falls in the same week
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS rose and RESIDENTIAL fell concurrently across all four observed weeks
regime_hint: spring seasonal transition during partial reopening
failure_condition: PARKS rises and RESIDENTIAL falls concurrently for two more weeks, yet RETAIL_REC's mean increases substantially over that period.
